mainTopic: The end of the משנה on lighter impurities for a נזיר. The גמרא then defines סככות and פרעות and asks whether ארץ העמים was decreed impure because of its air or its earth.
overview: The משנה finishes its list of lighter impurities. For these, a נזיר does not cancel his earlier days, starts counting again right away, and brings no קרבן. It adds an old tradition that the days of a זב, a זבה and a מצורע in הסגר still count toward his נזירות. The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה in אהלות to define סככות (overhanging trees) and פרעות (things sticking out of a fence). It then asks whether חכמים decreed ארץ העמים impure because of its air or because of its earth. It tries to prove 'earth' from the משנה's rule that the person is sprinkled on the third and seventh days. The proof is rejected: the sprinkling rule may refer only to some of the other items in the list. The גמרא supports this reading, since the list also includes vessels that touched a corpse, and a person who touches them does not need that sprinkling.

steps.title: The נזיר keeps his earlier days and brings no offering
steps.stepSummary: For the lighter impurities just listed, the נזיר does not lose his earlier days. He restarts his count immediately and brings no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not cancel the earlier days. He starts counting again right away, and he does not bring an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its ruling about a נזיר who became impure through the lighter impurities it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real טומאת מת makes a נזיר lose his earlier days and bring a קרבן. These lighter cases do neither. His days are kept, he picks up counting right after he becomes pure, and he owes no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: cancels or knocks down the days already counted
the earlier days of נזירות already counted
counts the days of נזירות
an offering brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: and he does not cancel the earlier days,
phrases.notes: "He" is the נזיר who became impure through the lighter impurities the משנה just listed.

phrases.english: and he starts and counts right away,
and he has no offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's ruling, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For lighter impurities, a נזיר keeps his earlier days, restarts his count immediately, and brings no קרבן.

steps.title: Days of זב, זבה and a confined מצורע still count
steps.stepSummary: An old tradition says that the days of being a זב or זבה, or a מצורע in הסגר, still count toward the נזיר's term.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth they said: the days of a זב and a זבה, and the days a מצורע is shut away, count for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an accepted tradition. Some kinds of impurity do not stop the נזירות days from counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule was about impurities that do not cancel past days. This tradition goes further: these days of impurity themselves count toward his נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: "in truth they said": signals an accepted, old tradition
a man or woman made impure by a bodily discharge
the waiting period when a possible מצורע is shut away
count toward

steps.whatToRemember: Lighter impurities don't cancel a נזיר's earlier days or require a קרבן. Days as a זב, a זבה, or a מצורע in הסגר even count toward his נזירות.

phrases.english: In truth they said:
the days of the zav and the zavah
and the days of confinement of a metzora,
these count for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule to close the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days of a זב, a זבה, and a מצורע in הסגר count toward the נזיר's term.

steps.title: Defining hangings and projections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in אהלות. סככות are a tree spreading over the ground, and פרעות are things sticking out of a fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These are the "hangings": a tree that spreads over the ground. And "projections": those that stick out from a fence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining two unclear words from the משנה, סככות and פרעות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה named these cases without saying what they are. The גמרא fills that in by quoting another משנה. A סככה is an overhanging tree, and a פרעה is something jutting out from a wall or fence.

keyTerms.meaning: "hangings": tree branches that spread over the ground
"projections": things sticking out from a fence
a tree
a fence or wall

phrases.english: GEMARA: And these are the "hangings" —
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting a משנה from אהלות to explain these words.

phrases.english: a tree that spreads over the ground.
And "projections": those that stick out from a fence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins by explaining terms from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סככות are overhanging trees, and פרעות are things jutting out from a fence.

steps.title: Was the land of the nations made impure because of its air or its earth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether חכמים decreed ארץ העמים impure because of its air or because of its earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the land of the nations." They asked: did they decree on the land of the nations because of its air, or perhaps because of its earth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, ארץ העמים, and raises an איבעיא about the reason behind the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the decree is about the air, just being there makes a person impure. If it is about the earth, he becomes impure only through the ground itself. The two sides lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: land outside ארץ ישראל
"it was asked of them": opens a question the חכמים raised
the air (being in the space)
a clod of earth (the ground itself)
they decreed (a rabbinic decree)

phrases.english: "And the land of the nations."
It was asked of them:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים, מִשּׁוּם אַוֵּירָא גָּזְרוּ עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: the land of the nations: did they decree on it because of its air,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא מִשּׁוּם גּוּשָּׁא גָּזְרוּ עָלֶיהָ?
phrases.english: or perhaps they decreed on it because of its earth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from defining סככות and פרעות to a new item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was the decree on ארץ העמים based on its air or on its earth?
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides whether merely entering ארץ העמים makes a person impure, or only contact with its ground.

steps.title: Attempted proof from the required sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה's rule that the person is sprinkled on the third and seventh days. It argues that if the decree were only about the air, sprinkling would not be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "And he sprinkles on the third and on the seventh day." If you say the decree is because of the air, why would sprinkling be needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 4 using a detail in our own משנה: the person needs sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that an air-based decree would not call for sprinkling on the third and seventh days. Since the משנה does require sprinkling, it suggests the decree is about the earth. Step 6 finishes this proof, and Step 7 rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: "come and hear": introduces a source to settle a question
sprinkles (the purifying water)
sprinkling for purification
"why do I need it?"

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And he sprinkles on the third and on the seventh day.
phrases.notes: This line comes from our own משנה, which says these impurities still need sprinkling.

phrases.english: And if you say it is because of the air,
why do I need sprinkling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the decree on ארץ העמים is about its earth, not its air.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that the person is sprinkled on the third and seventh days.

steps.title: So the decree must be about the earth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the proof from Step 5: since sprinkling is needed, the decree on ארץ העמים must be about its earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it because of the earth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion of the proof it began in Step 5. Because the משנה requires sprinkling, the decree must be about the earth of ארץ העמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the גמרא argued that an air-only decree would not call for הזאה. Here it closes the argument: the impurity must come from the earth itself. This line completes the proof, and the next step rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it…? (closes a proof by pointing to the only option left)
Clump of earth; the soil of the land itself

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because of the earth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the decree on ארץ העמים is because of its earth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule of sprinkling on the third and seventh days.

steps.title: The sprinkling rule may refer only to the other items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The decree could still be about the air, and the sprinkling rule in the משנה applies only to some of the other items listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. I can still tell you it is because of the air. When the משנה teaches the sprinkling, it is talking about the other items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof from Step 6. It says the sprinkling rule does not have to apply to ארץ העמים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the sprinkling rule covers every item in the משנה's list, including ארץ העמים. The גמרא says no: the rule may apply only to certain other items, such as the גולל, the דופק, and a רביעית דם. If so, nothing in the משנה shows that ארץ העמים needs sprinkling, and the decree can still be about the air.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (keeps the original idea despite the proof)
Air; the space over the land
On the rest; referring to the other items in the list

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying ארץ העמים is pure. It only says the sprinkling rule may not be talking about ארץ העמים.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ מִשּׁוּם אַוֵּירָא,
phrases.english: No, really I can tell you it is because of the air,
and when it teaches the sprinkling, it refers to the others.
phrases.notes: The 'others' are other items in the משנה's list, like the גולל, the דופק, and a רביעית דם.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ מִשּׁוּם אַוֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof completed in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. The question of air or earth stays open, and the air option survives.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed the sprinkling rule covers every item in the list, including ארץ העמים.

steps.title: Support: touching corpse-impure vessels needs no sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the rejection. The same list includes 'vessels that touch a corpse,' and a person who touches such vessels does not need sprinkling, so the sprinkling rule cannot cover every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, because the משנה teaches: 'and vessels that touch a corpse.' Do these vessels need sprinkling? Rather, learn from this that the rule refers to the others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for Step 7's reading of the משנה. It points to an item in the list that clearly does not need sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list includes 'vessels that touch a corpse,' and the גמרא assumes that a person who touches such vessels does not need הזאה on the third and seventh days. So the sprinkling rule cannot apply to every item in the list. That shows the rule was only about some of the items, which is exactly what Step 7 claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces support for the last answer)
Vessels that touch a corpse
Ones that need sprinkling
Learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: The sprinkling rule in the משנה does not cover every item in the list, so it proves nothing about ארץ העמים. The air-or-earth question is still open.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one rule stated at the end of a list does not always apply to every item in that list.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
since it teaches: 'and vessels that touch a corpse.'
Do these vessels require sprinkling?
phrases.notes: He means the person who touched such vessels; the גמרא assumes that person doesn't need the third-and-seventh-day sprinkling.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: it refers to the others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the rejection in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the sprinkling rule applies only to some of the items in the משנה's list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's inclusion of 'vessels that touch a corpse'; one who touches them does not need sprinkling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sprinkling rule refers only to some of the other items, so the proof that ארץ העמים was decreed impure because of its earth falls away.
